problems: For all five hypotheses, allele-specific binding is predicted in vitro rather than demonstrated by an allele-specific binding or perturbation assay.
The new GATA2 and RARA ChIP evidence supports occupancy near the variant in SK-N-SH, but does not establish allele-specific occupancy or causal enhancer regulation.
The element-to-LMO1 link is supported by contact and gene-prioritization evidence, but there is no reported CRISPR perturbation of the element; the eQTL is in skeletal muscle, not SK-N-SH.
The neuroblastoma allele and functional evidence specifically supports the GATA-motif route. It does not provide equivalent TF-specific phenotype support for RARA, TEAD4, FOXJ3, or ZNF8.
For H4 and H5, the supplied ChIP summaries report a peak in SK-N-SH without specifying that it is at or near the variant.

games.reason: The GATA2 model predicts stronger binding to ref C, and GATA2 is expressed with a SK-N-SH ChIP-seq peak whose summit is 32 bp from the variant. The literature’s opposite-strand G>T (equivalent here to C>A) weakens the first-intron GATA motif and is reported to reduce neuroblastoma initiation, so the binding direction and disease effect align. RARA also has an alt-favoring model and a nearby SK-N-SH ChIP-seq summit, but the supplied evidence does not connect RARA to the neuroblastoma effect or establish a downstream direction.

The GATA2 chain is better supported: its GATA2 model predicts stronger binding to ref C, and GATA2 is expressed and has a SK-N-SH ChIP-seq summit 32 bp from the variant. The literature also specifically connects the opposite-strand G>T change (equivalent to C>A here) to weakening a first-intron GATA motif and reduced neuroblastoma initiation. RARA has a nearby SK-N-SH summit and its family model predicts stronger alt-A binding, but the supplied evidence does not connect RARA specifically to the neuroblastoma mechanism.

The authors previously showed that overexpression of LIM-domain-only 1 (LMO1), a transcriptional coregulator, synergizes with MYCN to accelerate tumor formation and metastasis in an NBL-zebrafish model.
They now demonstrate experimentally, using genome-edited zebrafish, that a polymorphism in the human rs2168101 locus of the LMO1 gene determines which CRC is active in a tumor.
Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.
Thus, conversion of the regulatory GATA to a TATA allele in the first intron of LMO1 reduced the neuroblastoma-initiation rate by preventing formation of the adrenergic cell state.

Studies indicated that LMO1 plays a critical oncogenic role in various types of cancers, including T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, neuroblastoma, gastric cancer, lung cancer, and prostate cancer.

PMID 29760797 (2018): LMO1 super-enhancer polymorphism rs2168101 G>T correlates with decreased neuroblastoma risk in Chinese children.
Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.
Thus, conversion of the regulatory GATA to a TATA allele in the first intron of LMO1 reduced the neuroblastoma-initiation rate by preventing formation of the adrenergic cell state.
We found LMO1 rs2168101 G > T and rs11603024 C > T as well as LMO2 rs7933499 G > A were significantly associated with Wilms tumor risk.

Studies indicated that LMO1 plays a critical oncogenic role in various types of cancers, including T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, neuroblastoma, gastric cancer, lung cancer, and prostate cancer.
The rs2168101 G>T polymorphism observed in the LMO1 gene is located at a conserved GATA transcription factor binding motif.

We confirmed that rs2168101 G>T was significantly associated with decreased neuroblastoma risk for both northern and southern Chinese children and the combined subjects [GT vs. GG: adjusted odds ratio (OR)=0.57, 95% confidence interval (CI)=0.44-0.74, P<0.0001; TT vs. GG: adjusted OR=0.29, 95% CI=0.15-0.56, P=0.0002; GT/TT vs. GG: adjusted OR=0.53, 95% CI=0.41-0.68, P<0.0001; and TT vs. GT/GG: adjusted OR=0.36, 95% CI=0.19-0.69, P=0.002] after adjustment for age and gender.
